name: EmergencyFund

custom.system_prompt: You are generating conversations which focus on budget planning.

initial_prompt: Create a collaborative conversation that focuses on planning the budget and discussing future expenses and savings.

setting.relationship_dynamic: Friends helping each other improve financial habits
setting.background: One person has little cash available for unexpected expenses

scenario_template.topic: Discussing the purpose of an emergency fund
scenario_template.note: They talk about unexpected repairs, medical bills, or income disruptions

scenario_template.topic: Finding room for savings in the current budget
scenario_template.note: Most monthly income is already allocated

scenario_template.topic: Choosing a reasonable emergency savings target
scenario_template.note: They ask how to start with small contributions
Assistant explains how regular transfers can build the fund gradually

scenario_template.topic: Finding expenses that can temporarily be reduced
scenario_template.note: They compare optional spending with the importance of financial security

scenario_template.topic: Handling occasional months with higher expenses
Agreeing on their first emergency savings milestone
scenario_template.note: They celebrate having a concrete starting point

user1.name: User1
user1.role: Person who is motivated to manage their finances more effectively but has limited experience with budgeting and can become overwhelmed when faced with many expenses, financial categories, competing priorities, or unexpected costs.

user2.name: User2
user2.role: Person who is organized and detail-oriented, willing to help track and plan finances, but tends to overthink spending decisions, double-check calculations, and seek confirmation when deciding how to allocate money across competing needs.

assistant.name: Assistant
assistant.role: Budget planning assistant that provides clear, structured, and practical guidance for organizing expenses, setting spending priorities, creating realistic budgets, and tracking progress, while suggesting alternatives when income, savings goals, recurring costs, or unexpected expenses constrain the available budget.
